answer: One concrete defense is staked identity with slashing. To act, an agent must lock a bond in escrow, and each new identity starts on a hollow reputation record. Copying one agent into a thousand clones does not multiply credibility: every copy posts its own collateral, so attack cost scales linearly with fake identities instead of staying flat. When peers flag a clone cluster on a shared mesa of weighted votes, the protocol slashes the cluster at once, turning the Sybil farm into a net loss. Reputation earned slowly over attested work is the ivory-tower asset that cannot be minted in bulk.
